list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden on PlayStation until earned, no online trophies.

sources.advice: Every guide below is this entry's own words, reasoned from the official descriptions; where a description does not pin a detail down, the guide says so.
sources.officialList: Exophase, Grand Theft Auto VI Trophies - PS5 (exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/) — official names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them.
sources.targets: PSNProfiles, Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi) — the counts PlayStation tracks, shown as 0/target.

trophies.guide: The platinum, and the only trophy with no task of its own: it pays the moment the other 54 are earned. Use this tracker as the checklist — when the header reads 54 of 55 with only this one left, the next trophy you earn, whichever it is, completes the set. If you are planning the run, plan for A Long Road (100% completion) last; it is the trophy everything else feeds into.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission — the game starts here, so this is simply a matter of playing the introduction to its end rather than stopping at the first free-roam moment. Nothing in the mission is scored or timed for the trophy; completion is all it asks. Expect it inside the first hour, and treat the mission as the tutorial it is: the partner and driving basics it teaches are the same ones later trophies lean on.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 of the campaign. Chapter trophies pay on completion, not performance, so play at your own pace and use the chapter to learn Leonida's map — the areas you unlock here are where the first stranger strands and activities appear. Before the chapter closes, make your first manual save: the three-save rule on the Missables tab starts here.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. The name is printed with asterisks by PlayStation itself — that is the official spelling, not a redaction by this guide. Keep a fresh manual save at the chapter's start, and if the chapter offers explicit story choices, let them register: Actions Speak Louder counts choices across the whole game (PlayStation tracks 500), and story chapters are where they cluster.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. By now the map and the activity menu are largely open, which makes this the natural point to start Master of None in the background — try each new activity type once as the story introduces it, rather than in a dedicated session later. Rotate your manual saves at the chapter start as before.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter before the endgame. Completion is all that is asked. After this chapter the final mission is ahead, so this is the last relaxed moment to bank progress on the cumulative counters — stunts, challenges, choices — before you decide whether to finish the story or sweep the open world first. Either order works; nothing in the chapter trophies closes behind you.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish the campaign's final mission — one of only two gold trophies on the list. Save manually before you start it: the endgame is where the choice-flavoured trophies (Actions Speak Louder above all) are most likely to be decided, and a pre-finale save costs nothing. The trophy pays on completion regardless of how the mission goes moment to moment, and free roam continues afterwards for everything else on this list.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run when the campaign offers it. Like the other named-mission trophies, it pays on completion with no medal or time requirement. Mission trophies cannot be skipped past — the campaign routes through them — so the only way to miss one is to stop playing the story.
trophies.name: Trust
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish The Cartel Heist, a set-piece story mission. It pays on completion. Heist-style missions are also where the game teaches the robbery loop that free-roam trophies later repeat — bank vaults, armored trucks, gang operations — so pay attention to the escape half of the mission; losing the heat cleanly is a skill this list asks for again and again.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. A completion trophy on the campaign's path: no score, no timer, nothing extra hidden in the description. Keep playing the story and it arrives in order.
trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. As with the other named missions, the trophy is for completing it, however the run goes. If a mission ever defeats you repeatedly, remember the list's own joke trophy, Bad Luck, I Guess — a failed first attempt followed by success is a pattern this game rewards elsewhere too.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the airport authority in Leonida's world, and the same location returns in Catch Me If You Can, which asks for an unscheduled departure from VCIA in free play — learn the layout while the story walks you through it. The trophy itself pays on mission completion.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Finish Operation Savage Glory, a named story mission. Completion pays the trophy. Large set-piece missions like this one are the best early source of Combat Focus practice — Gunslinger asks for 5 takedowns inside a single use of it, and crowded story fights give you the targets to learn the timing before you hunt it deliberately.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's own completion counter — PlayStation tracks it as 0/100, and this is the second of the two golds and the real length of the platinum. The counter is the game's, not this list's: story, strands, activities and collectibles all feed it in proportions the game decides. Work it last, with the tracker's unearned filter as your cleanup list, and check the in-game completion page rather than guessing which category is short — the counter, not the trophy count, is what has to reach 100.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/100: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts — the jumps and stunt moments the game counts, tracked 0/250 by PlayStation. This is a mileage trophy, not a skill wall: it fills in while you cross Leonida for other trophies, especially during the collectibles stage. If it is short at cleanup time, work the stunt jumps area by area rather than driving at random — a stunt only counts when the game registers it, so a clean landing matters more than a spectacular crash. One of six silvers, and the one most players will finish without noticing.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/250: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity once — PlayStation tracks 9 types. This is the tour trophy: ranges, races, fishing, arcade games, hunting and the rest of Leonida's side menu, one attempt each, win or lose. Do it early. It costs an afternoon, it teaches you which activities the silver and gold grinds will ask you to master, and several of its stops (the shooting range above all) are much easier to enjoy in small visits than in one 42-challenge sitting later.
trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/9: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the count is PlayStation's own, 0/42. Medals are scored per challenge, so this is 42 small exams rather than one big one: learn a challenge's target pattern, retry it while it is fresh, and move on the moment the gold lands. Spread the work out — a few ranges per session from the moment the story first takes you to one. Saving all 42 for the end is how this silver becomes the longest single grind on the list.
trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/42: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 of them, tracked by the locations you have won at rather than a raw win count. A win at a new location is progress; a win at an old one is practice. Learn each course's line with a first run, then race it in earnest — drone races reward memorised turns far more than reflexes, and the courses do not change between attempts.
trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/14: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the operative word: the same race won twenty times counts once. Work across the race menu instead of farming a favourite, and count a new event each session. Vehicle choice and a clean first lap matter more than aggression; a race you finish second in teaches you the course for the win that counts.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/20: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal — a named character — in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the 9 activity types, so you will meet the mechanics on the Master of None tour; Cal's challenge is the competitive version of it. The official description does not say where Cal fishes, and this guide will not invent a spot: take every fishing challenge the game offers as strands and activities open up, and Cal's is the one with his name on it. Win once and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the description names no location, so none is claimed.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet the world offers. Not start one — complete one, which is the only wrinkle: pick the shortest game on the cabinet for your first completion. It is also one of the 9 activity types, so it doubles as a stop on the Master of None tour.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger strand — every mission Andy gives you, through to the final one. Stranger strands unlock as the story opens the map, and each named character's strand pays its trophy only at the end, so a strand started is a strand to finish in the same few sessions while its story is fresh. Andy is one of the five named strands; Strangers & Freaks needs eight finished strands in all, so Andy alone is not enough.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand through its final mission. The pattern is the same as every named strand: take Kenton's missions whenever the marker is up, and do not leave the strand half-done while you tour the map — strands are short, and their finales are where the trophy sits. Counts toward the eight strands Strangers & Freaks asks for.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger strand through its final mission. Billy's is one of the five named strands on the list; finish it and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks as well. If a strand's later missions do not appear, progress the story — strands are gated by the campaign opening new areas and contacts.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish 8 stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida — PlayStation tracks 0/8. The five named strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus Bret's hunting strand make six; the remaining two come from the unnamed strands the map offers, which is why the guide's advice is simple: never drive past a stranger marker. A strand counts when it is finished, not started, so keep strands short and closed rather than many and open.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/8: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger strand through its final mission — the strand's name, Supply & Demand, is the trophy Randy pays under. Same rule as the other named strands: the trophy is at the end of the strand, and the strand counts toward the eight that Strangers & Freaks requires.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger strand through its final mission. Tyrone is the fifth named strand; with Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy done, the named set is complete and Strangers & Freaks needs only the strands the map offers beyond them. Finish strands in the order the story unlocks them and none of them can be left behind.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — 18 of them, tracked 0/18. A visit-the-spot collectible: the work is travel, not difficulty, so fold the spots into the exploration stage and clear them region by region alongside the WAiNK locations and the 52 areas of The Goodtime State. When a spot is somewhere scenic and elevated, that is the pattern — the list rewards looking at the map's edges, not its centre.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/18: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for, as part of Bret's stranger strand. A unique animal means a specific one, not any animal of the species: follow the strand's own tracking beats rather than hunting at random, and take the shot the strand sets up. Hunting is also one of the 9 activity types, so Bret's strand doubles as your Master of None hunting stop.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets — sets, not cards: PlayStation tracks 0/3 completed sets. This is the only collectible on the list with an internal structure, so track it by set from the first card you pick up: a card's value to you depends on which of its set-mates you already hold. Three sets is far short of every card in the game, so once your third set closes, the rest are optional — check your nearest set before any long detour.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/3: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Use a WAiNK point at 100 different locations — 0/100 on PlayStation's counter, and one of the six silvers. Like the meditation spots, this is a travel trophy: the interaction itself is trivial, the map is the cost. Clear locations region by region during the collectibles stage, and let the counter in this tracker tell you when a region is done — 100 is too many to hold in your head.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/100: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's Challenges — tracked 0/50. Challenges are the small scored tasks the world and its activities generate; the count is cumulative and forgiving, because 50 completed challenges is a fraction of what a full playthrough attempts. Check the counter before grinding: most players find this one pays during the activities stage without a single dedicated session.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/50: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, reach a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape — both halves, in that order, together. The partner is the game's second protagonist, so this is a single-player trophy despite the wording; the list has no online trophies at all. Earn the stars somewhere with an escape route — near tunnels, alleys or a vehicle swap — and stay together while the heat dies: separating from your partner is the easy way to fail the 'with your partner' half.
trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time — the opposite discipline from Hot Together: here the heat must not die between shops. Pick three shops close together, rob the first, drive — don't hide — to the second and third, and let the escape come only after the third register. A fast car staged outside the first shop is the whole strategy; the trophy is a route-planning test dressed as a crime spree.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — 0/100, and 'discover' in these lists means encounter and drive, not buy. The counter fills fastest in varied traffic: rich districts, docks, airfields and rural roads all spawn different pools. Make a habit of stealing the first example of anything you do not recognise for one block; by the collectibles stage you will be most of the way there without a single dedicated drive.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/100: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies inside one activation of Combat Focus, the game's slow-motion combat state. The requirement is a crowd and a plan: trigger Focus when at least five enemies are already in the open and in range, and work nearest-to-farthest so nobody leaves the arc. Crowded story set-pieces and gang operations are the natural hunting ground — attempt it there first, where the game gathers the targets for you, rather than provoking a crowd in free roam.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA — the airport — in an unscheduled way: get airborne or out of the field by a route no timetable offers. VCIA appears in the story (VCIA Takedown), and the trophy wants you back there in free play, taking a plane that was never yours to take. The official description does not name an aircraft, so neither does this guide: any departure the airport did not schedule is the shape of it, and escaping the response afterwards is part of the fun rather than the requirement.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the description names the place (VCIA) but no vehicle, so none is claimed.

trophies.guide: The description is a joke with the vehicle named inside it: a Rhino is the series' tank, and this trophy is about your time in one — 'kinda hot in these Rhinos' is the whole official text. The list gives no count and no target, so treat it as a set-piece moment: when the game puts you in or against a Rhino, stay in the moment rather than fleeing it. Because PlayStation hides this one, expect it during a story or strand set-piece rather than in free roam.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the official description is a single joke line, and the guide says no more than it supports.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and stay undetected doing it — the stealth entry in the crime set. Undetected means the robbery completes before anyone raises the alarm, so go in quiet: no drawn weapon on entry, no lingering, and an exit that does not pass a crowd. If the first attempt gets loud, the stores reset — this is repeatable in free roam, and the clean run usually comes once you know a store's layout from the loud one.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each — tracked 0/5, and one of the six silvers. A vault robbery is the full loop: entry, the vault, the take, and losing the response. Only escapes count toward the five, so a robbery that ends in arrest is practice, not progress. Vary the banks as you go; the robbery the story teaches (The Cartel Heist) is the template, and free-roam vaults repeat it at rising heat.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/5: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape — a single clean job, unlike Maximum Withdrawal's five. Armored trucks are tougher than their cargo is heavy: stop or breach the truck, take what it carries, and be gone before the response organises. The escape is part of the requirement, so plan the getaway before the robbery, not during it.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — PlayStation tracks 52 areas, 0/52. The frame trophy for the whole collectibles stage: meditation spots, WAiNK locations, cards and vehicles all live inside these 52 areas, so clear area by area and let this counter certify the sweep. The last areas are always the map's edges — islands, swamps and the far coast — so when the count stalls, stop searching the middle.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/52: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — 9 gangs, tracked 0/9, so nine robberies, one per gang, and repeats on the same gang do not advance it. Keep a list: the tracker counter tells you how many, not which, so note the gangs as you clear them. Gang operations sit in gang territory, which makes this the natural partner of the exploration stage — rob as you reveal each gang's ground.
trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/9: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail somewhere with a view on Ocean Beach — the list's most relaxed requirement and the one its name winks at ('In The Beginning…' is a series in-joke about starting over somewhere sunny). Go to Ocean Beach, find the spot that serves drinks with the ocean in front of you, and take the moment. It is a one-off: minutes, once you are standing in the right neighbourhood.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, in a vehicle, 'in classic style' — the classic style being through the glass rather than through the door. Take a car from inside a showroom and exit through the storefront. It is a one-off moment trophy: any showroom, any car, one dramatic exit. Expect a wanted level for your trouble; the trophy pays on the smash, not the escape.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go bowling at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — the alley is named in the description, and 'follow-through' is the bowling term the trophy wants you to honour: play the game there, properly, rather than merely visiting. Bowling is also the kind of stop the Master of None tour rewards, so pair them: one visit, two trophies' worth of progress.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately cryptic — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and PlayStation hides this trophy, which together mark it as a specific story-flavoured moment between the two protagonists rather than a repeatable activity. It is flagged on the Missables tab for exactly that reason: one-off moments cannot be farmed if the moment passes. Play the partnership content as the story offers it, keep your chapter saves, and if it has not paid by the credits, revisit the Missables advice before starting the 100% cleanup.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged from its official description: a single named moment ('a partnership with mass appeal'), hidden on PSN, with no count and no repeatable activity attached. If the moment is a one-time story beat, it can be passed — keep a manual save at each chapter start so you can return for it.
trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the description is cryptic by design, and the guide claims no more than it supports.

trophies.guide: Make choices — PlayStation tracks them, 0/500, which makes this the strangest counter on the list: five hundred registered choices is far more than any single story's branching points, so choices here must include the small ones the game logs as you play (dialogue picks, approach choices, decisions in strands and activities). Play naturally, choose when asked rather than skipping, and watch the counter: it should climb steadily. It is flagged on the Missables tab because a choice, once made, cannot be unmade in that playthrough — the counter is why the three-save rule exists.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged from its official description and its PSN counter: choices are permanent once made, and the trophy counts them to 500. If any required choices sit behind a branch you did not take, only an earlier save reaches them — save at chapter starts and before explicit story decisions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/500: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second attempt at something that defeated you the first time — 'second time's the charm' is the whole official description, and the trophy is hidden on PSN. Read plainly, it wants a fail followed by a success at the same thing: a mission, a race, a challenge. Do not go out of your way to manufacture it early; a long playthrough produces genuine second attempts on its own, and the trophy will name the moment when it happens. It is flagged on the Missables tab in case the qualifying attempt belongs to a one-time event.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged from its official description: a second attempt implies a first one that failed, and if the attempt in question is a one-time story event, passing it first try — or failing it twice — could close the trophy. Chapter saves are the insurance; do not reload away a first failure until you know whether the retry paid.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the description is a single joke line, and the guide says no more than it supports.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the list's UFO-flavoured entry, hidden on PSN and described only by the reaction it wants from you. Trophies worded this way in this series pay for stumbling onto one of the world's scripted oddities: an unexplained sight, an event that is not part of any mission. There is no counter and no map marker to chase; explore at night, follow up the weird rumours strangers tell you, and do not rush past anything the game slows down to show you.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own; the description names no place or event, so none is claimed.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down with a melee drive-by — swing a melee attack from a moving vehicle and connect with someone on foot, ten-pin style. Low speed is your friend: too fast and you simply run them over, which is a different crime and not this trophy. A quiet street, a slow roll, one well-timed swing. It takes a few attempts to learn the range; the failures cost nothing.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Advice: this guide's own, from the official description.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 worth of Marked Bills through your contacts — PlayStation tracks the dollars, 0/250000. It is a throughput counter, not a savings goal: money you launder counts forever, even after you spend it, so route every marked bill the crime trophies earn you through your contacts instead of spending it raw. Robberies and gang operations are the income; this trophy is the habit of cleaning them. It will usually complete during the money stage without a dedicated grind.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/250000: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops — tracked 0/100000, cumulative, and deliberately easy to finish late: clothes, weapons, vehicles and services all count, across every shop rather than in one. Do not force it early by buying things you do not want; a full playthrough spends this many times over. If it is somehow short at cleanup, the garage properties of Little Boxes are the biggest single purchases left to make.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/100000: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties — tracked 0/8. This is a purchase trophy, so the only requirement is the money and the tour: garages are bought where they stand, spread across Leonida, and each one also gives your vehicle collecting a home. Buy them in the money stage, after the story's income and the laundering habit are established, and the eight purchases also pour most of Treat Yo Self's $100,000 into its counter.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/8: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — tracked 0/10. Registration is the app's record of a vehicle as yours, so the rhythm is: find a vehicle worth keeping, drive it, register it. Pair it with Whip It Good's 100 discoveries — every tenth discovery or so, register the best of the bunch — and both counters finish inside the same habit.
trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.sources: Official name, description and grade: Exophase's GTA VI (PSN) trophy list. Tracked target 0/10: PSNProfiles' GTA VI trophy list. Advice: this guide's own.
